analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: The page covers free fall in a vacuum under gravity, constant acceleration and its equations for velocity and displacement, a time table showing linear and quadratic growth, and Galileos findings including air resistance effects.

overview.headline: Free fall under gravity with constant acceleration and motion equations

keyPoints.point: Object falling through vacuum is subjected to only gravitational force expressed as weight
keyPoints.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.

keyPoints.point: Acceleration is constant and equal to gravitational acceleration of 9.8 meters per square second at sea level
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyPoints.point: Velocity increases linearly and location increases quadratically under constant acceleration
keyPoints.quote: Notice that the acceleration is a constant, the velocity increases linearly, and the location increases quadratically.

keyPoints.point: Galileo proposed that all free falling objects fall at same rate nearly 400 years ago
keyPoints.quote: The remarkable observation that all free falling objects fall at the same rate was first proposed by Galileo, nearly 400 years ago.

keyTerms.gloss: motion caused only by gravity with no other forces acting on the object
keyTerms.quote: is said to be free falling and its motion is described by Newton’s second law of motion.

keyTerms.gloss: acceleration that remains constant at sea level due to gravity
keyTerms.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: velocity measures rate of motion from initial location over time
keyTerms.quote: where a is the acceleration, V is the velocity, and X is the displacement from an initial location.

keyTerms.gloss: displacement is distance from initial location along motion path
keyTerms.quote: where a is the acceleration, V is the velocity, and X is the displacement from an initial location.

keyTerms.gloss: drag force is resistance from atmosphere acting on moving object
keyTerms.quote: If the object falls through the atmosphere, there is an additional drag force acting on the object
